subject: Orion Health: Private deployment onboarding - network evidence & path to go-live
messages:
From: Ben Turner <ben.turner@orionhealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@orionhealth.com, procure@orionhealth.com
Date: 2028-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy - network evidence & KMS placement question

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving forward internally and the security team has asked for a short package of network evidence and a couple of clarifications before we can get a procurement PO issued. Can you help with the following items?

1) A current network connectivity diagram showing VPC peering/Transit/VPN connections to our on-prem environment (or confirmation of IP ranges we should expect to peer with).
2) A short doc describing how KMS keys are handled for Redwood Private (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed).
3) SOC2 summary for the inference control plane and any network isolation attestations you have.
4) A proposed cutover window and high-level runbook for onboarding (we expect a staging validation then production cutover).

Also, are there MTU/port requirements or known egress destinations we need to whitelist on our firewall? Our security lead is in copy (ops@orionhealth.com). Procurement (procure@orionhealth.com) will be pulling the PO once the compliance pack is complete.

Appreciate a rapid turnaround — do you have the items today or early tomorrow?

Best,
Ben Turner
Senior Cloud Engineer
Orion Health

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: ops@orionhealth.com, procure@orionhealth.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - network evidence & KMS placement question

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear list. We can supply everything you need. Attaching our Private Onboarding checklist (PDF) that maps to the items you asked for and the expected owner for each artifact.

Quick answers up front:
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS in your cloud account is supported and preferred for EU deployments; Redwood Private can be configured to use a customer KMS key (we provide key ring and grant templates).
- Ports/MTU: Typical requirements are TCP 443 outbound to Redwood-managed slices; no special MTU expected (> 1500 is fine). For peerings we recommend BGP over VPN/Direct Connect and allow UDP 123 for NTP.
- SOC2: attaching a 1-page SOC2 summary; we can provide the full report under NDA.

Next steps I propose: 1) intake call with your network/security next week to validate CIDRs and peering method, 2) we exchange sample IAM/service-account manifests for the service accounts we ask you to create, 3) staging validation window (2 hours) then production cutover (1 hour).

I'll loop in Karthik (network lead) — Karthik, can you review the checklist and call out anything missing for our EU on-prem flow?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182
(attachment: redwood_private_onboard_checklist_v1.pdf; soc2_summary.pdf)

Hi team — quick technical notes based on the checklist Stephanie attached. Ben, if you can confirm the items below we can prepare the exact manifests and the peering playbook.

Requested confirmations from Orion Health:
- CIDR(s) you plan to present for peering (we prefer /20 to /24 ranges for logical isolation).
- Preferred peering method: AWS Transit Gateway / Direct Connect / VPN (or cloud-agnostic equivalent).
- Will your KMS be in a customer-managed key ring in the same region as the Redwood Private control plane? (This affects key policy examples.)
- Service account model: do you prefer a single cross-account role for all nodes or per-node service accounts?
- Egress policy: do you require allow-listing only to specific IP ranges or do you run an egress proxy?

Operational checks we will run during staging:
- BGP adjacency and route propagation validation
- TLS handshake and certificate chain verification for mutual TLS where applicable
- KV cache replication and metrics smoke (to ensure model loading works across the peered path)

Attachment: I will add an abbreviated network-playbook (internal) to the onboarding folder once we confirm CIDRs.

Thanks — Karthik.

Marcus, Priyom: looped you for procurement/elbow-grease on the runbook and IP allow-list templates.

Thanks Karthik — answers below and attaching our diagram.

- CIDRs: 10.48.0.0/20 for app-tier, 10.49.0.0/24 for management. We can present additional /24s if needed.
- Peering: we prefer Direct Connect / Transit gateway. Initial staging will use VPN with BGP; production will be Transit Gateway via DX.
- KMS: Keys will be customer-managed in our EU region KMS; they will be created in the same account as the Redwood Private VPCs.
- Service account model: we prefer a single cross-account role for Redwood services to assume (easier for audit).
- Egress: our firewall team wants explicit allowlisting to known Redwood egress IP ranges. We attached a diagram and a procurement contact (procure@orionhealth.com).

Attachments included: orion_net_diagram_v2.png (network diagram), procurement_contact_card.vcf

We can do an intake call Thursday 2028-04-13 at 10:00 AM BST (that is 02:00 AM PDT — sorry timezone pain; 10:00 BST / 11:00 CEST). Does that work for your EU network folks?

Ben
